We need a clear write-up on how Redwood defines and measures SLOs for uptime and latency, plus a pragmatic plan for how customers can access metrics during the procurement evaluation.

Specifically we need:

- Alerting behavior: what triggers an alert, how alerts map to incidents, and on-call escalation flow.

- Temporary carveout: Acme legal wants a short-term exception process while we validate metrics — e.g., 30-day read-only access for procurement team with controls.

Can you send a short packet (2–3 pages) plus any sample dashboards or a matrix we can attach to our procurement questionnaire? If you need to loop in product/ops, please do.

Hi Jordan — thanks for the scope. Adding the technical details below and attaching a dashboard snapshot. I'm keeping the language procurement-friendly.

Summary of how we measure and surface SLOs (concise):
- Uptime (availability SLO):
  - Definition: percentage of successful API connections (2xx/3xx) to a pinned model endpoint over a rolling 30-day window.
  - What counts as failure: 5xx responses, connection timeouts (>5s for establish + TLS), and throttling that exceeds configured rate limits per account.
  - Aggregation: 1-minute buckets aggregated to 24-hour windows for trend & 30-day rolling window for SLO.

- Latency (p95 / p99 request latencies):
  - Definition: 95th/99th percentile of server-side request duration (time from request arrival to first byte of model response) for production traffic, excluding synthetic/healthcheck traffic.
  - Sampling & retention: full per-request telemetry stored at 1s resolution for 14 days; p95/p99 computed daily and stored as metrics for 365 days.

- Evidence sources & monitoring systems:
  - Primary: Prometheus-compatible metrics (ingest pipeline to TSDB), request logs in secure object storage, and our inference runtime traces (Jaeger).
  - Retention: raw logs 30 days, metrics (aggregates) 365 days by default.

- Alerting & incident mapping:
  - Alert triggers: sustained deviation from SLO > 5% for 15m (severity: P2), or complete endpoint unavailability for 5m (severity: P1).
  - On-call & escalation: Ops on-call receives page -> triage -> incident created in our PagerDuty (or customer's preferred bridge) -> post-incident report within 72 hours for P1.

- Customer access options (procurement-friendly):
  - Option A (Snapshot): PNG/PDF dashboard snapshot + exported metric CSVs (good for procurement review).
  - Option B (Read-only): Short-lived read-only Grafana link scoped to Acme's account and IP allowlist; access is logged, revoked automatically after the window.
  - Option C (API): Time-limited API token for metric exports (s3/CSV), subject to NDA and entitlements.

Temporary carveout proposal (what we do for evaluation):
- We will provision a 30-day read-only Grafana link, scoped to up to 5 Acme emails and two IP ranges. Access will be audited; downloads are logged.
- If you need more than 30 days, we'll convert to a contractual entitlement with a data access addendum.

Attachments included:
- grafana-dashboard-snapshot.png (UI snapshot of relevant panels)
- grafana-live-README.txt (how to connect and what each panel means)

Note on sampling/edge cases: we exclude synthetic load and retries flagged by the client SDK from SLO calculations; we also apply standard outlier removal for cold-start spikes during deploy windows. Happy to detail the exact PromQL queries if you want.
